title: Reflection's 501B open-weight Beam — compute counted, weights pending
summary: Reflection announces Beam, a 501-billion-parameter open-weight model claiming a third to a quarter of a rival's compute, and the show works out what that claim counts and leaves out. Then why almost nobody can budget for tokens, from a paper on cheaper models that cost more, and how OpenAI's new EU text watermark hides a signature in word choices.

topics: Reflection's Beam: 501B total / 23B active open-weight (Apache 2.0) MoE, weights promised 'later this month' after red-teaming; '3-4x less inference compute' than GLM 5.2 computed as 2 x active params x mean generated tokens, excluding prefill, attention and serving overhead; active-parameter ratio alone (40/23) is ~1.7x, so the rest must come from shorter generations; Reflection's own table puts Kimi K3 ahead; $4.7B raised, $25B pre-money, >$7B SpaceX/Nebius compute, Shinsegae sovereign 'AI factory'

Why AI token spend can't be budgeted: WSJ (via PYMNTS) says ~11% of ~400 businesses could project AI costs; the Price Reversal paper (Chen, Stoica, Zaharia, Zou et al.) finds lower-list-price models cost more in 32% of pairs, up to 28x, with up to 9.7x thinking-token variation on repeated runs of the same query; Accenture: one in three exhausted annual token budgets, 54% of requests over-tiered; Epoch: median OpenAI researcher coding-agent spend ~34-day doubling; SemiAnalysis: Anthropic subscriptions ~5x API-equivalent value, OpenAI halved its $200 plan's value and added $500 tier

OpenAI's EU text watermark (textGrain) for ChatGPT and Codex under the AI Act transparency rules: green-list watermarking (Kirchenbauer et al. 2023) explained; 10% synonym replacement drops detection from ~92% to 66%; detector limited to approved researchers; API off by default; absence of watermark proves nothing; OpenAI's shelved 2024 watermark and regulation removing the first-mover penalty

dives.story: Reflection's Beam and what its compute claim counts
dives.why_it_matters: Teams choosing an open-weight base for private deployment need to know the 3-4x efficiency claim counts generated tokens and excludes the prefill and attention that dominate agent workloads, before the weights even land.

dives.story: Why nobody can budget for tokens
dives.why_it_matters: Finance and platform teams setting AI budgets need to know that list price misranks actual cost a third of the time and that the same query can vary nearly tenfold, so they should budget ranges and measure cost per finished task.

Anyone publishing, teaching or building on model text in the EU now meets a watermark whose detector is restricted and easily weakened by editing, so knowing what it can and can't prove matters before anyone relies on it.

concepts_taught: mixture-of-experts compute accounting: total parameters set memory, active parameters set per-token arithmetic, and inference FLOPs ~ 2 x active params x generated tokens, so efficiency claims split into a model-size term and a verbosity term

green-list text watermarking (Kirchenbauer et al. 2023): a keyed random split of the vocabulary at each step, a soft bias toward green tokens, detection by counting greens with a statistical test; weak on low-entropy text like math, short passages, paraphrase and translation
